_meta.description: Domain-agnostic field-definition schema for core bibliographic and high-level structural metadata from scientific documents.
design_principles: Constraints are used only where they improve normalization without harming extraction quality.
Most fields remain unconstrained to preserve robustness for LLM-based extraction.
The schema defines target metadata fields only; response formatting and provenance are handled separately.

title.description: Main title of the scientific document itself.
instructions: Copy the document title verbatim as printed on the first page or running header. Preserve casing and punctuation.

subtitle.description: Subtitle of the document, if explicitly given.

affiliations.description: Institutional affiliations associated with document authors.
instructions: One entry per distinct affiliation, in order of first appearance. Do not repeat affiliations.
Assign IDs in sequence: aff_1, aff_2, aff_3, etc.

label.description: Local marker used in the document, such as a superscript number, letter, or symbol.
instructions: Copy the printed superscript or symbol exactly as printed, e.g. '1', 'a', '†', '‡'. Use null if no explicit label is given.

text.description: Affiliation text as given in the document.
instructions: Copy the full affiliation address verbatim, including department, institution, postal code, city, country.

authors.description: Authors of the scientific document in document order.
instructions: Extract document authors only.
Preserve author order as it appears in the document.
Assign IDs in sequence: author_1, author_2, author_3, etc.

full_name.description: Full author name as presented in the document.
instructions: Copy as printed. Use initials if the document prints initials; full names if it prints full names. Do not expand initials.
Extract only ORCID identifiers explicitly associated with the author.
Return ORCID as the bare identifier without URL prefix, e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097.

is_corresponding.description: Whether the author is explicitly marked as a corresponding author.
instructions: Use true if the author is explicitly marked as a corresponding author (asterisk, footnote, 'Corresponding author' label). Use false otherwise.

affiliation_refs.description: References linking the author to affiliations.
instructions: Use the exact id values assigned in the affiliations list (e.g. aff_1, aff_2).
Use [] if the author has no affiliated institution.

abstract.description: Main abstract of the scientific document.
instructions: Copy the printed abstract verbatim.
Do not include graphical abstracts, highlights, or keyword lists.
Extract explicit keywords only.
Do not infer keywords from the abstract or body text.

doi.description: DOI of the document itself, if explicitly given.
instructions: Extract only the DOI that belongs to the document itself.
Do not extract DOIs from cited references.

arxiv_id.description: arXiv identifier of the document, if explicitly given.
instructions: Extract only the arXiv ID that belongs to the document itself.
Use the unversioned bare arXiv ID, e.g. '1812.03956' not '1812.03956v1'.
Do not extract arXiv IDs from cited references.

url.description: Canonical URL of the document, if explicitly given.
instructions: Extract only a URL that points to the document itself.
Do not extract URLs from cited references.

publication_date.description: Publication date of the document in the most precise form available.
instructions: Extract the publication date for the document itself, not dates from cited references.

If multiple dates are present, use this priority order: (1) final journal publication date; (2) online publication date; (3) accepted date; (4) revised date; (5) received date; (6) manuscript-printed publication date (e.g. a '(Dated: ...)' line inside the PDF); (7) arXiv submission date (use the version stamped on the PDF being annotated); (8) copyright year.
When two dates of the same priority level appear, use the later one.
Use the most precise date available in the selected source: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, or YYYY.
Do not combine dates from different sources. If only a year is available for the highest-priority source, use that year rather than a more precise lower-priority date.

venue.description: Primary scholarly venue or container of the document, such as a journal, conference, workshop, proceedings venue, or repository.
instructions: For arXiv preprints, use arXiv.
For published versions, use the journal/conference name as printed.
Use null if no venue indicator is printed.

publisher.description: Publisher or issuing organization of the document.
instructions: Publisher name as printed in cite line, footer, or copyright notice (e.g. 'American Chemical Society', 'Elsevier'). Use null for arXiv-only papers.

language.description: Primary language of the document content.

constraints.format: ISO 639-1 two-letter code, e.g. en, fr, de.

funding.description: Funding information explicitly stated in the document, restricted to entries with both an identifiable funder and an explicit grant or award identifier.
instructions: Create a funding entry only when the document gives both an identifiable funder and an explicit grant or award identifier for it.
Create one entry per (funder, grant_id) pair:
- if a funder gives multiple grants, create one entry per grant_id;
- if a single grant has multiple co-funders, create one entry per co-funder.

Do not create an entry for a funder, institution, or acknowledgment named without an explicit grant or award identifier (e.g. general thanks to an institution, vendor, or a fellowship/position with no award number).
The identifier must be a funding grant or award number; do not use identifiers that are not tied to financial support.

funder.description: Funding organization name associated with the grant.
instructions: Use the funding organization name as printed; use the full name if printed, and the acronym only when no full name is given.
When both the full name and its acronym are printed, use the full name and omit the acronym.
If no funding organization is named but a funding programme, scheme, or project is named as the source, use that programme, scheme, or project name as the funder.

grant_id.description: Grant or award identifier explicitly given in the document.
instructions: Single grant ID exactly as printed.

If the printed identifier includes an associated project, programme, or acronym alongside the grant or award number, preserve the full printed identifier phrase as written, e.g. '834134 (WATUSO)' or 'SIONA,C14/22/099'.

section_headings.description: Top-level headings of the main scientific body in reading order.
instructions: List the explicit top-level headings of the main scientific body in reading order, exactly as printed (preserve numbering, capitalisation, punctuation).
Exclude front matter (Abstract) and back matter (Acknowledgements, Funding, Author Contributions, Conflict/Competing Interests, Data Availability, References/Bibliography).
Exclude subsection headings, metadata blocks, and figure/table captions.
Exclude supplementary materials, supporting information, and appendix sections (both the section heading itself and any headings within them).

has_references.description: Whether the document contains a references or bibliography section.

has_figures.description: Whether the document contains one or more figures.

has_tables.description: Whether the document contains one or more tables.
